correctness.rationale: For every one of the 65536 Boolean tables the finite 32-state successor permutation is explicitly formed, giving a bijective representation of de Bruijn cycles by exactly 2048 one-cycle masks. A cross-join is exactly a double toggle of distinct tail bits with alternating conjugate positions; the package independently checks that criterion against validity of each doubly switched mask for all 245760 candidates. Complete BFS from every valid mask covers all 2096128 unordered pairs and proves the exact distance and eccentricity distributions. Actual replay from crossjoin_verify.py returned VERIFY_OK; all required data are contained in the package. The matching published degree histogram supplies an independent graph-construction checksum.

originality.rationale: The specific new claim is the complete graph-geodesic histogram, radius, diameter and eccentricity distribution of the 2048-vertex order-five cross-join graph. The original cross-join theorem proves connectivity and the 2018 full paper gives degree distribution and Hamiltonian paths, none of which implies the exact geodesic statistic. The 2020 usage of diameter measures conjugate-position span, not number of cross-join operations. The accessible earlier local claim concerns clique number. Results were compared by mathematical implication rather than title or parameter match; unavailable full texts are retained as historical-priority risks.

value.rationale: The metric solves a natural operational question left open by connectivity: the worst and typical number of validity-preserving two-switch feedback modifications required to convert one maximal-period order-five shift register to another. An exact seven-move diameter, full distance histogram, and center/eccentricity census classify the whole 2048-cycle benchmark and are not implied by the earlier degree or clique information. The theorem states no unsupported higher-order or cryptographic application.
